This page defines the operator workflow for moving a PAGe candidate from an
untouched prospective holdout to a deployable frozen kit. It describes the
required artifacts and checks. A local frozen acceptance replay has now been
completed for run ID `boundary-expansion-20260801T150000Z`; its candidate
failed the locked NLL gate, so no refit or promotion followed. The private and
disclosure-safe evidence is ignored by Git under `results/`.

## Four-phase chain

| Phase | Input state | Required action | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Frozen acceptance | Candidate and incumbent kits were both trained without `2025-26` | Replay both frozen kits on the same authorized `2025-26` observations and metric definitions | Candidate and incumbent replay results |
| 2. Immutable decision evidence | Both replays are complete | Apply the locked `check_promotion()` gates and bind the decision to hashes of the data and both kits | Private decision bundle plus disclosure-safe audit evidence |
| 3. Fixed-spec refresh | Phase 2 passed | Refit the accepted candidate configuration with `2025-26` released into training; do not search or select a new specification | Private refreshed training result plus disclosure-safe manifest |
| 4. Registry and verified loading | The refresh and every preceding link validate | Copy the refreshed kit to an immutable registry entry and write its deployment manifest | Hash-bound promoted kit loaded only through `load_promoted_kit()` |

Each arrow is one-way. Never replace an earlier artifact in place, and never
infer a release from a bare `pass = TRUE` value. The hashes and manifests bind
the exact data, candidate, incumbent, decision bundle, refreshed artifact, and
promoted kit used in the chain.

## Before the holdout: development and retuning

Model search belongs before Phase 1. The preferred low-level path starts with
`validate_season_selection()`, with `2025-26` in `holdout_seasons`, and then
runs the guarded lifecycle in order:

```text
tune_m0 -> validate_m0_tuning -> fit_m0 -> freeze_m0
tune_m1 -> validate_m1_tuning -> fit_m1 -> freeze_m1
tune_m2 -> validate_m2_tuning -> fit_m2 -> freeze_m2
assemble_kit -> validate_page_kit
```

M1 cannot consume a draft M0, M2 cannot consume a draft or mismatched M0/M1,
and governed kit assembly checks the exact upstream identity chain.

`train_pipeline(mode = "retune")` is the high-level compatibility orchestrator
and now composes the guarded lifecycle. It may use compatible prior tuning
results to build a bounded grid, retain the current v16-corrected incumbent, add local
neighbors, and expand a boundary reached by the previous winner. Whichever
interface is used, freeze the selected candidate and record its training
seasons before examining `2025-26`.

With `previous_results`, `plan_m2_grid()` consolidates finite NLL by stable
specification identity and falls back to finite fold scores when the summary is
missing. Prior IDs must be unique and exactly match their parameter-derived
canonical IDs; Bernoulli NLL is preferred to `mean_nll`, and ties rank by the
canonical ID. The planner retains the v16 incumbent and best prior
specification, preserves diverse finalists, adds local neighbors, and expands
a winning boundary using its adjacent observed spacing, subject to the explicit
grid cap.

Looking at holdout outcomes and then changing a grid, specification, feature,
threshold, or correction rule starts a **new development cycle**. The resulting
model is not validated by the decision made on the model that was previously
frozen. Do not rerun the same `2025-26` data and describe the result as a new
untouched confirmatory evaluation.

Before freezing, inspect every tuned axis for a boundary winner. Expand a
winning edge by one adjacent valid step while retaining the incumbent, winner,
and local neighbors; or document why the edge is a meaningful null or hard
constraint. A computational cap leaves an unresolved boundary and does not
prove an optimum. The stage-specific procedure and stopping rules are in the
[tuning playbook](tuning-playbook.md).

The governed API enforces this ordering at runtime: `train_pipeline(mode =
"retune")` checks M0 boundaries before starting M1, then calls
`validate_m1_tuning(check_boundaries = TRUE)` before freezing M1 or starting M2.
An unresolved non-null edge now stops the run immediately with the parameters
named in the error, so downstream compute cannot be spent on a candidate that
must be retuned.

This differs from the Phase 3 refresh. A post-acceptance refresh keeps the
accepted M0, M1, M2, and runtime settings fixed and only refits them after the
passing decision explicitly releases `2025-26` into the training seasons.

The final full-LOSO selection rule is also an explicit user choice:

| `selection_method` | Rule |
|---|---|
| `"min_nll"` | Lowest Bernoulli NLL, then complexity and specification ID |
| `"one_se"` | Simplest candidate within one standard error of the best NLL; requires finite fold-level scores |
| `"pareto"` | Non-dominated on NLL, worst-horizon MAE, and worst-phase MAE; final tie order is NLL, complexity, then specification ID |

## Phase 1 and 2: frozen replay and decision evidence

Use one authorized data snapshot and two pre-holdout kits:

```{bash}
Rscript scripts/acceptance/replay_2025_26.R \
  --data=/secure/PAGe/authorized_surveillance.csv \
  --candidate-kit=/secure/PAGe/candidate_pre_holdout.rds \
  --incumbent-kit=/secure/PAGe/incumbent_pre_holdout.rds \
  --private-output=/secure/PAGe/acceptance-private \
  --audit-output=results/audit \
  --season=2025-26 \
  --run-id=<unique-acceptance-run-id>
```

The command rejects either kit when its recorded training seasons include
`2025-26`. It replays both kits through the same frozen path and applies the
canonical locked promotion thresholds.

Canonical `m2_production` identity is required by default. When an incumbent
has only the historical `m2` field, add
`--kit-compatibility=legacy_m2`; this explicit compatibility mode warns and is
also required in the refit and promotion commands. Conflicting canonical and
legacy fields are always rejected.

`--private-output/<run-id>/` contains row-level replay RDS files and
`decision_bundle.rds`. Keep it in authorized private storage. The decision
bundle records the run and holdout identity, the canonical gate report, and
SHA-256 hashes for the authorized data and both kits.

`--audit-output/<run-id>/` contains aggregate metric and diagnostic CSV files,
`decision.md`, and the disclosure-safe `result_manifest.json`. The manifest
also hashes the private decision bundle. Review the aggregate files before
moving to Phase 3; disclosure-safe means row-level surveillance and replay
objects are excluded, not that review can be skipped.

Both run directories must be absent at start. Reusing a run ID fails rather
than overwriting evidence. A failing gate still saves its evidence and then
exits nonzero. The acceptance command has no training side effect.

## Phase 3: fixed-spec refresh including 2025-26

Validate the full Phase 2 binding without starting training:

```{bash}
Rscript season2526/run_retrain_venkata.R \
  --data=/secure/PAGe/authorized_surveillance.csv \
  --promotion-bundle=/secure/PAGe/acceptance-private/<run-id>/decision_bundle.rds \
  --promotion-manifest=results/audit/<run-id>/result_manifest.json \
  --candidate-kit=/secure/PAGe/candidate_pre_holdout.rds \
  --incumbent-kit=/secure/PAGe/incumbent_pre_holdout.rds \
  --output-dir=/secure/PAGe/refit-private \
  --manifest-dir=results/post-promotion-manifests \
  --preflight-only
```

Remove only `--preflight-only` to perform the refresh. The script verifies the
decision and manifest schemas, locked thresholds, pass status, source hashes,
candidate and incumbent training seasons, candidate specification identity,
authorized-data hash, and the presence of `2025-26` in the authorized input.
It constructs artifact-bound evidence with `verify_promotion_evidence()` and
then calls `train_pipeline(mode = "refresh", promotion = evidence)` with the
accepted candidate settings. A bare `check_promotion()` report cannot release
the holdout.

Before saving, the script requires the holdout status to be `released`,
`2025-26` to appear in the refreshed training seasons, and the M0, M1, M2, and
runtime configuration to match the accepted candidate. It does not retune.

`--output-dir` is private and receives a hash-qualified
`post_promotion_refit_*.rds`. `--manifest-dir` is separate and receives its
disclosure-safe RDS and Markdown manifest. Existing artifact or manifest names
cause failure; the script never overwrites them.

## Phase 4: immutable promotion registry

First validate the complete chain without copying a kit:

```{bash}
Rscript scripts/promotion/promote_post_refit.R \
  --data=/secure/PAGe/authorized_surveillance.csv \
  --acceptance-bundle=/secure/PAGe/acceptance-private/<run-id>/decision_bundle.rds \
  --acceptance-manifest=results/audit/<run-id>/result_manifest.json \
  --candidate-kit=/secure/PAGe/candidate_pre_holdout.rds \
  --incumbent-kit=/secure/PAGe/incumbent_pre_holdout.rds \
  --refit-artifact=/secure/PAGe/refit-private/post_promotion_refit_<hashes>.rds \
  --refit-manifest=results/post-promotion-manifests/post_promotion_refit_<hashes>_manifest.rds \
  --registry-dir=/secure/PAGe/deployment-registry \
  --audit-dir=results/deployment-audit \
  --deployment-id=<unique-deployment-id> \
  --preflight-only
```

Remove only `--preflight-only` to register the kit. The command writes the
private kit to
`--registry-dir/<deployment-id>/promoted_kit.rds` and writes the
disclosure-safe `deployment_manifest.json` and Markdown summary under
`--audit-dir/<deployment-id>/`. It creates no mutable `current` alias. A
collision at either destination fails before anything is replaced.
`--deployment-id` may be omitted to generate an ID from the run time and refit
manifest hash.

Load a registered kit by passing both immutable paths:

```{r}
library(PAGe)

kit <- load_promoted_kit(
  kit_path = "/secure/PAGe/deployment-registry/<deployment-id>/promoted_kit.rds",
  deployment_manifest_path =
    "results/deployment-audit/<deployment-id>/deployment_manifest.json"
)
```

`load_promoted_kit()` validates the disclosure-safe
`promoted_deployment_kit` manifest, verifies the promoted-kit SHA-256, checks
the recorded specification and training seasons against the kit, and then
validates the kit schema. It has no default path and does not discover a
mutable latest artifact.

For lower-level tooling, `read_result_manifest(path)` reads and validates
canonical JSON or RDS manifests. `write_result_manifest(manifest, path,
overwrite = FALSE)` validates before and after writing and refuses an existing
path by default.

## Evidence and disclosure boundary

| Location | Classification | Typical contents |
|---|---|---|
| Acceptance `--private-output` | Private | Row-level candidate/incumbent replays and decision bundle |
| Acceptance `--audit-output` | Disclosure-safe | Aggregate metrics, diagnostics, decision summary, result manifest |
| Refresh `--output-dir` | Private | Full refreshed training result and model objects |
| Refresh `--manifest-dir` | Disclosure-safe | Training seasons, spec identity, row counts, and source hashes |
| Promotion `--registry-dir` | Private | Immutable deployable kit |
| Promotion `--audit-dir` | Disclosure-safe | Deployment manifest and summary |

The repository intentionally does not contain the authorized surveillance
snapshot or a completed instance of these private artifacts. A source document,
example path, or successfully rendered page is not evidence that the governed
workflow ran.

## Public synthetic smoke

The following bounded command exercises acceptance, fixed refresh, immutable
promotion, manifest validation, and verified loading with synthetic fixtures:

```{bash}
Rscript scripts/public/synthetic_release_workflow.R --smoke
```

Temporary outputs are removed by default. Pass
`--output-dir=<new-disclosure-safe-directory>` to inspect them; an existing
destination is rejected. This smoke check tests workflow plumbing only. It does
not fit or validate the real PAGe forecasting model and does not show that any
private `2025-26` operation occurred.
